newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Content and editing decisions determine TV jurisdiction.
newsitem.headline: Content and editing decisions determine TV jurisdiction.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday that television broadcasters established in more than one member state come under the jurisdiction of the state where decisions on programming and editing are taken.

A Belgian court has asked for clarification under the European Union's TV without frontiers directive to determine if the television station VT4, broadcast via satellite from Britain, should be considered British or Belgian.
VT4's programming is directed at the Flemish community over cable in Belgium and is not seen in Britain.

The court's ruling today strengthens VT4's programming opportunities in Belgium by telling the Flemish government there is nothing in the treaty on European Union that prevents a British broadcaster from offering a programme in Belgium and not in Britain.
The Flemish argued that VT4 is Flemish, and banned from cable programming under an 18-year broadcasting monopoly between the Flemish government and competitor VTM (Vlaamse Uitgeversmaatschappij NV).

The court's ruling directs the Belgian court to review where the broadcasting company is legally established, and if there are two legal entities to look at where decisions as to programming policy and final editing are made.

une decision a titre prejudiciel sur l'interpretation de la directive 89/552/CEE du Conseil, du 3 octobre 1989 visant a la coordination de certaines dispositons legislatives, reglementaires et administratives des Etats membres relatives a l'exercice d'activites de radiodiffusion televisuelle (JO L 298, p. 23)
THE COURT hereby rules

L'article 2, paragraphe 1, de la directive 89/552/CEE, du 3 octobre 1989, visant a la coordination de certaines dispositions legislatives, reglementaires et administratives des Etats membres relatives a l'exercise d'activites de radiodiffusion televisuelle, doit etre interprete en ce sens qu'un organisme de radiodiffusion televisuelle releve de la competence de l'Etat membre dans lequel il est etabli. Lorsqu'un organisme de radiodiffusion televisuelle est etabli dans plus d'un Etat membre, la competence dont il releve revient a l'Etat membre sur le territoire duquel l'organisme de radiodiffusion a le centre de ses activites, notamment la ou sont prises les decisions concernant la politique de programmation et l'assemblage final des programmes a diffuser.
